description: Hi everyone! I'm a software developer skilled in full-stack development, AI, mobile apps, and DevOps, with experience in Python, Laravel, React, Next.js, and Flutter. For NASA Space Apps 2026, I'm focusing on Flame in Freefall, using AI and NASA data to improve space fire safety. I'm looking for passionate teammates skilled in AI/ML, data science, physics, UI/UX, or software development. Let's combine our talents, innovate, and build something impactful together!
summary:
Fire behaves differently in space. Changes in gravity, oxygen concentration, and pressure create unique combustion challenges that can threaten astronauts and future missions to the Moon and Mars. Although NASA has conducted decades of combustion research, its scientific findings are distributed across multiple experiments, reports, and data sources.

**IGNIS AI** is an AI-powered research dashboard developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge's *Flame in Freefall* challenge.

Our platform helps researchers **summarize scientific studies, compare experimental measurements, interpret findings with traceable citations, and rank relevant investigations** based on specific space mission conditions.

IGNIS AI combines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), scientific data visualization, and a transparent, weighted Mission Advisor. NASA combustion research supports the document knowledge base, while available external measurements are clearly identified.

By transforming complex scientific evidence into accessible, mission-relevant insights, IGNIS AI aims to support better-informed spacecraft fire-safety research and identify critical knowledge gaps for future human space exploration.
details:
IGNIS AI — Project Details

The Problem

Fire safety is one of the critical challenges of human space exploration. In microgravity and reduced-gravity environments, flames can behave differently from those on Earth. Oxygen concentration, atmospheric pressure, airflow, and material properties can significantly influence ignition, flame spread, and extinction.

NASA has conducted extensive combustion research through experiments aboard the International Space Station and through ground-based and lunar research programs.

However, relevant findings are distributed across scientific publications, experimental records, measurements, and technical documentation. Identifying which findings apply to a particular spacecraft or habitat scenario can require substantial research effort.

Our Solution

IGNIS AI is an interactive, AI-powered scientific research dashboard designed to make combustion evidence more accessible, understandable, and relevant to human space exploration.

Our platform integrates four essential capabilities:

1. Summarize Scientific Research

IGNIS AI organizes combustion investigations and retrieves relevant scientific information from indexed NASA research documents.

2. Compare Experimental Data

Researchers can explore experimental measurements, compare recorded conditions, visualize trends, and export available data while preserving original measurement units and source information.

3. Interpret Scientific Evidence

Our AI research assistant uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to answer research questions using scientific documents and evidence citations.

It can distinguish document passages, structured measurements, and qualitative visual observations.

4. Rank Mission-Relevant Evidence

Our Mission Advisor helps researchers identify investigations relevant to specific mission conditions, including lunar habitats, Martian habitats, spacecraft, and space stations.

Users can specify an environment, research objective, oxygen concentration, pressure, and optionally a fuel type.

The ranking engine evaluates investigations using seven transparent factors: objective, fuel, oxygen, pressure, experimental outcome, evidence quality, and gravity relevance.

Unlike a conventional AI chatbot, this ranking is calculated through deterministic code rather than generated by a language model.

NASA Scientific Resources

IGNIS AI's research knowledge base incorporates material from important NASA combustion research programs:

  • ISS Researcher's Guide to Combustion Science: Background on combustion science, microgravity investigations, and research facilities aboard the International Space Station.
  • SoFIE — Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction: Research into material ignition, flame growth, extinction, and suppression in reduced gravity.
  • FLARE — Flammability Limits at Reduced-g: Research into material flammability limits and how reduced gravity affects spacecraft material screening.
  • FM2 — Flammability of Materials on the Moon: Research into combustion and material flammability under lunar-gravity and exploration-atmosphere conditions.

Additional NASA historical safety resources provide context for the importance of spacecraft fire-safety research.

The initial structured numerical dataset used for experimental comparison comes from external ZARM flame-spread research and is explicitly labeled as external. Importing and validating additional numerical datasets from NASA Physical Sciences Informatics is part of our development roadmap.

Technical Implementation

IGNIS AI uses a full-stack research architecture:

Frontend

  • React 19, TypeScript, and Vite
  • Tailwind CSS for interface design
  • Recharts for scientific data visualization

Backend

  • Python and FastAPI
  • REST API for scientific data exploration, analysis, and AI operations

Database and Search

  • PostgreSQL 17 with pgvector
  • Vector-based semantic search
  • 768-dimensional document embeddings

Artificial Intelligence

  • Ollama for local AI inference
  • Llama-based models for research assistance
  • Gemma-based vision models for image interpretation
  • Nomic embeddings for scientific document retrieval
  • Optional NVIDIA NIM inference

Scientific Processing

  • Python and SQL for numerical comparisons and deterministic ranking
  • PDF document extraction and indexing
  • Image and video analysis with qualitative evidence records

What Makes IGNIS AI Innovative?

IGNIS AI goes beyond a traditional AI chatbot.

It combines scientific document retrieval, numerical analysis, multimodal evidence interpretation, and explainable mission-specific ranking in one research environment.

Scientific measurements are stored and calculated independently of the language model. Generated explanations remain linked to their supporting sources.

The system preserves important distinctions between NASA-linked research, external experimental data, and unverified observations.

Instead of hiding missing information, IGNIS AI reports evidence coverage and limitations.

Impact

IGNIS AI aims to help combustion researchers, aerospace engineers, and students:

  • Discover relevant scientific evidence more efficiently.
  • Compare experimental findings across available conditions.
  • Understand which studies are relevant to particular mission scenarios.
  • Identify missing evidence and opportunities for further research.
  • Support informed investigation of fire safety for future Moon, Mars, and spacecraft missions.

Limitations and Future Development

IGNIS AI is a research prototype, not a certified fire-safety system.

Its relevance scores are not probabilities of fire, and its recommendations do not certify materials or predict suppression success.

Our next development priorities include importing reviewed NASA numerical experimental datasets, expanding evidence coverage, strengthening human verification of scientific sources, and collaborating with combustion experts to validate ranking methodology.

Our vision is to make scientific evidence easier to discover, understand, and apply to the challenges of safer human space exploration.
